articles.title: Houseplant hacks: should you always quarantine new plants to avoid pests spreading?
articles.summary: Any new addition to your collection can contain stowaways, so you’d be wise to deploy a little patience – but how long is long enough? The problem There is nothing quite like the joy of bringing home a new plant.
body: The hack Quarantining means keeping any new plant separated from the rest of your collection for a few weeks before letting it join the others. The logic is simple: if something is going to emerge, you want it to do so in isolation, where it can be dealt with before it spreads to the whole crew.

The method Place your new plant in a different room from the rest of your collection for two or three weeks. Every few days, check for webbing, sticky residue, tiny moving specks, or gnats rising from the compost. Treat any pests while the plant is isolated, and only move it in with the others once you are confident it is clean.

The test I have been quarantining new plants for several years now, and it works. New arrivals have come in with the odd stowaway, but because they were isolated, whatever they brought stayed contained to that one pot rather than becoming everyone’s problem.

The verdict Nearly every serious infestation I have seen, my own included, traces back to a new plant being introduced straight into your home collection. Quarantining is not a sign of paranoia; it’s the best way to protect your plants, and it costs nothing but a little patience.
articles.author: Gynelle Leon

articles.title: Transylvania beyond the spooky castles: a family adventure in Romania’s mountains
articles.summary: Forget the vampire tales – the Eastern Carpathians deliver dramatic peaks, roaming bears and deep solitude. As the sun disappears behind the high tree line, our campfire spits and crackles.
body: “This area is very wild,” says Samir Teslovan, who drove us up through the densely forested peaks from his guesthouse in Toplița. “When I come here to the mountains, I charge my battery, charge my soul. I feel free, like the wind.”

Sitting on the edge of a fragrant forest of spruce, fir, beech and pine, our view stretches over the valley to misty mountains receding in layers to the horizon. Samir points to a far-off peak in the east, a pyramid on a ragged ridge. “That’s Ukraine, maybe 200km,” he tells us. Then, pointing west: “That way, 400km, is Hungary.” The forest is still home to bears, wolves and lynx, but it’s the solitude that brings him here. “I prefer wild zones, where no one goes,” he says. “There are places here that nobody knows.”

Across the vast forests and mountains of Harghita County in central Romania, there are many places that nobody knows. In fact, the whole region has flown under the radar of international travellers – 85% of visitors come from Romania itself, which feels bizarre when you discover the wonders here, as we did on a 12-day family road trip, staying at self-catering lodges and cabins along the way.

articles.title: Student bank accounts: don’t be swayed by the freebies, freshers told
articles.summary: Sign-up perks may capture the attention but should the focus be on the interest-free overdraft? The best student deals and discounts. An insider’s tips on student money.
body: I n the scramble to sort out university accommodation, join freshers group chats and work out how a student loan payment is meant to stretch across a whole term, there is one big decision that is easy to put off but worth getting right: which student bank account to open.

Student accounts work like any other current account but come with two extras that don’t apply to the general public: an interest-free overdraft, and a lot of perks designed to hook you in as a customer for life.
However, while it is tempting to choose an account on the strength of the free cash, vouchers or other goodies, personal finance experts advise you not to be swayed by the extras.
“An interest-free overdraft could provide greater value over the course of a degree than a one-off freebie,” says Caitlyn Eastell at Moneyfactscompare.co.uk.

articles.title: Max Rocha’s recipes for confit trout salad and grilled courgette with apricot, stracciatella and roasted almonds
articles.summary: Two Café Cecilia stalwarts that are just the thing for the summer heat. Five years after Café Cecilia opened, a handful of dishes have become permanent fixtures, returning to the menu time and again – and this confit trout salad is definitely one of them.
body: First, make the pickled cucumber by combining 100ml water with the sugar, vinegar and salt in a saucepan, then gradually increase the heat until the sugar dissolves. Pour this over the cucumber and radishes in a bowl, and set aside.
Season the trout, then leave to sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, place the sunflower oil, olive oil, thyme and garlic in a pan and heat to 50C (122F) (if you don’t have have a kitchen thermometer, the outside of the pan should feel warm to the touch). Pat the trout dry with kitchen paper, then lay the fish in the warm oil and keep it between 50-55C (120-130F) for 15-20 minutes, until cooked through. Leave to cool a little, then peel off and discard the skin (this is easier to do while the fish is still warm) and leave to cool fully.

Combine the olive oil, mustard and white-wine vinegar. Drain the pickles, then put in a bowl with the watercress and one and a half tablespoons of the vinaigrette (save the rest for other salads in the week). Mix and taste for seasoning, then add a squeeze of lemon juice, a few extra drops of olive oil and a pinch of sea salt and black pepper as required.

articles.title: 24 Best Bridal Pajamas for the Wedding, Honeymoon, and Beyond
articles.summary: You have the dress—now, shop Vogue’s edit of the best bridal pajamas, sets, and robes to ensure you start your wedding day on the right foot.
body: The big white dress gets a lot of attention—but in the run-up to your big day, you start to realize exactly how many bridal extras you may need. From the rehearsal dinner to the bridal shower to, yes, the loungewear you’ll wear to sip your coffee and get ready the morning-of, weddings come with a lot of outfit changes. Why not have fun with it? Bridal pajamas take on many forms—and the best ones, complete with feather embellishments and silky fabrics, are really pretty fabulous.

Think of it as your way to set the tone for the day. Choose a satin robe to match an opulent setting, a breezy cotton set to mirror a coastal destination, or a beautifully detailed slip dress that makes you feel put-together just by throwing it on. One thing to keep in mind: Whatever sleepwear you choose, opt for something you can slip on or off without compromising your hair and makeup.

Whatever you gravitate to, it’ll serve as a memento of your special morning long after the day is done; choose wisely. From perfectly bridal pajama sets to sweet robes to delicate nightgowns both long and short, here are 24 options to consider.
articles.author: Lea Donenberg

articles.title: Dylan Meyer and Shatara Michelle Ford on Remaking Genre Movies in Their Own Image
articles.summary: The filmmakers behind “The Wrong Girls” and “Dreams in Nightmares” have reimagined two classic tropes—the buddy comedy and the road movie—for a different time (and different bodies).
body: When I tell filmmaker Shatara Michelle Ford that I don’t want to pin down Dreams in Nightmares, their elegiac sophomore feature, explicitly as a “road movie”—that it feels too slippery, too much its own thing, to sit neatly inside a genre built on decades of lone men and empty highways—they stop me, considerately.

“I appreciate you not wanting to put it in a genre bucket,” they say. “But the whole thing that I do is a revisionist exercise with all things. So this is a revisionist road movie. It’s definitely that.”

“I like to think of the obvious, Hollywoodized, uncomplex version of the thing that I’m trying to do, and then I intentionally undo it,” Ford explains. “Not that I would have made the Hollywood version anyway. I’m having a conversation with that the whole time.”

A few weeks earlier, Dylan Meyer was describing a similar instinct in her own directorial debut, The Wrong Girls —a profane, druggy stoner comedy about two aimless best friends who accidentally steal a suitcase stocked with vials of an experimental drug. There are talking cats, Dutch criminals, and telepathy. The protagonists, notably, are women.

articles.title: ‘Look in the mirror. That’s the trick’: our fashion expert Jess Cartner-Morley answered your questions
articles.summary: The Guardian’s fashion editor on tips for the well-dressed man to the ethical issues of fast fashion, how to wear jewellery and whether Andy Burnham looks good. PetertheGray asks: Why are so many high end items made from synthetic fibres? And are synthetics always bad?
body: The answer to the first part of your question is just, price. As to the second part - as a rule of thumb, natural fibres are a sustainable choice. Virgin polyester - which is made from oil, and doesn’t biodegrade - is to be avoided. But there are also sustainable synthetic fibres. Look out for Tencel, which is the most common brand name for a fabric called lyocell, which is made from wood pulp, and is biodegradable.

I commend both of you for having figured out what you like and what suits you. That’s the hardest part. My personal bugbear front-fastening trousers where the ‘hidden’ hook-and-eye fastening is too close to the edge of the fabric so the metal keeps showing. Drives me insane.

articles.title: The Exec’s Guide to Longevity Tech
articles.summary: AI is reshaping preventative health just as longevity becomes one of luxury’s fastest-growing opportunities. Where is the technology heading next, and what should fashion execs be paying attention to?
body: Living longer is the new luxury. Once confined to biotech labs and the disposable income of Silicon Valley billionaires, longevity is no longer a tech bro hobby and has become a consumer aspiration in its own right. Preventative full-body MRI scans, AI-powered health dashboards and wearable biometric trackers are rapidly moving from niche health tools to status symbols, particularly among affluent consumers and celebrity ambassadors.

The CEOs of many of the leading players in the space say their fastest-growing consumer categories are Gen Z and post-menopausal women. For the ultra-rich, healthspan — the proportion of one’s life spent living in good health — has become one of the few remaining assets that money can meaningfully improve.

articles.title: The Saint-Tropez Scene May Seem Impenetrable—Here Are Our 10 Unwritten Rules for Making the Most of It
articles.summary: There are laws, and then there is protocol.
body: Brigitte Bardot may be gone, but the mythology she unwittingly created in Roger Vadim's 1956 And God Created Woma n still defines how the world imagines Saint-Tropez: a world of sun-kissed shores, seduction, and carefree abandon. But that enchantment began long before the beach clubs and celebrity sightings. Back in 1892, French artist Paul Signac dropped anchor here, encouraging friends such as Henri Matisse and André Derain to follow. And in the 1920s, weary of Paris, the writer Colette settled near Plage des Salins, finding joy in picking figs and lemons from her garden, dancing at open-air balls with young sailors—and eventually declaring she'd found paradise.

Today's cast of characters is more likely to include billionaires, influencers, and a new generation chasing the White Lotus fantasy. Yet Saint-Tropez remains stubbornly itself, with social rituals and unspoken conventions that aren't always obvious at first. Knowing them won't just help you avoid the occasional faux pas; they'll help you navigate the village like a pro.
La Réserve à la Plage is a more demure beach club option, at least aesthetically.
articles.author: Lanie Goodman

articles.title: The 15 Most Beautiful Airport Landings in the World, Ranked
articles.summary: Flying to any of these destinations? You'll want to bag a window seat.
body: Whether you’re a seasoned jetsetter or a first-time flier, few things compare to the bird's-eye vista that comes into focus during the most beautiful airport landings in the world. While the long-legged aisle-hoggers among us might not relate, travelers lucky enough to settle into the window seat on certain flight routes can look forward to quite the show ahead of touchdown.
Plane travel is the only means of transport onto and off the island for all tourists and locals on Lord Howe Island, New South Wales, Australia.

To uncover the most beautiful airport landings in the world, AllClear Travel Insurance analyzed 32 airports around the world known for the dazzling views ahead of the runway. One hundred participants were presented with a series of images showcasing the airport runways, and their visual engagement was measured using eye-tracking technology to determine the most captivating landings. The speed at which participants first focused on an image, and the average length of time participants spent looking at each image, were both recorded and turned into a score.
